tasks.task: Build a bank of the person's own work stories

items.when: Before a CV or interview, when the person has done good work but cannot find examples on the spot
When the person has work notes, to turn them into impact statements backed by evidence
When a target role is known, to map real work history to what the role needs
When the person lists duties and cannot see which of their experience counts as evidence

tasks.task: Rewrite a CV or resume

items.when: When a CV must be rewritten using only the person's own history
When you want a second, paste-ready version and a flaw report to compare with yours
When a long CV must come down to two pages without losing the point
Before sending, to see what hiring software may miss in the layout and keywords
When the CV is drafted, to read it as a busy recruiter and list what they would skip

tasks.task: Tailor a CV to one job ad

items.when: Before tailoring, to split the ad into firm needs, wishes and what is missing
When the CV must answer one ad without inventing anything
When you want a guided run from the ad to a tailored draft and application answers
When you want other bullet wordings and a keyword map to choose from
Before sending, to see every claim the person's record cannot support

tasks.task: Write a cover letter for one job

items.when: When the tailored CV is done and the letter must add the why, not repeat the CV
When a standard letter feels flat, to try a short numbered letter that ends in a proof
When CV and letter are drafted, to check both for claims the history does not support
When a line could be in anyone's letter, to test it and get a true, specific rewrite

tasks.task: Answer selection criteria and application questions

items.when: When a form asks how the person meets each criterion within word limits
Before answering, to pick the story that best proves each criterion
When an answer is over the word limit and must lose words, not evidence
Before submitting, to check each answer rests on something the person really did

tasks.task: Prepare a person for one interview

items.when: When an interview is booked and likely questions need answers from the person's own stories
Before prep, to see the questions and the strong and weak answer signs an interviewer may use
When the person knows little about the employer, to plan what to find out and where
When answers must be short examples tied to the role, with practice questions
When an answer is a list of claims and needs one true incident that shows the point

tasks.task: Run a mock interview and give feedback

items.when: When the person wants a script to practise with and notes on each answer
When you need a realistic question set with what a good answer shows
When the role is technical, to practise at a chosen pressure level and get scores
When you have written feedback on the answers, to check it is specific and usable

tasks.task: Prepare a talk for an interview presentation task

items.when: When the brief and audience are known, to get a storyboard and then the slides
When the outline is agreed and the person needs a clean deck fast
When there are two or three ways to open the talk, to have a fresh reader pick one
When the deck is drafted, to check slide count, time and type size

tasks.task: Write thank-you and follow-up messages after an interview

items.when: The same day as an interview, and again if nothing is heard by the date given
When the note should name one true, specific thing and ask for nothing
Before sending, to catch a misspelt name, title or company

tasks.task: Rewrite a LinkedIn profile

items.when: When a profile must say clearly what the person does and who they help
Before writing, to settle what the person wants to be known for and by whom
When you want another headline and About section to compare with yours
When the headline is a job title and needs several honest angles to choose from
When the profile is drafted, to read it as a recruiter or client and list what is unclear

tasks.task: Write a professional bio in three lengths

items.when: When the person needs a one-line, a short and a full bio that agree with each other
When the one-liner will be spoken, to try 10, 30 and 60 second versions
When a consultant sounds like everyone else, to find the one plain line they can own
When the bio says passionate and results-driven, to swap each for a fact

tasks.task: Write a speaker one-sheet and a host introduction

items.when: When a speaker needs topics, a bio and an intro the host can read aloud
When the one-sheet needs a layout, to see three directions at real size and pick one
When the sheet needs one short proof story from past work
Before it goes to organisers, to tie each credit, client name and number to a source

tasks.task: Write a freelance marketplace profile and bid replies

items.when: When the profile must say what the freelancer does, for whom and with what result
When past projects must become short case studies that show the person's role
When replying to a posted job, to write a bid tied to something specific in the brief
When a client asks for a price, to set scope, assumptions and contract risks
Before setting a rate, to check it covers the monthly income the person needs

tasks.task: Plan LinkedIn posts and outreach for a job search

items.when: When the person wants to be seen, to set topics and a posting rhythm they can keep
When a real work story should become a post the person publishes themselves
When one idea should be tried in two voices before posting
When the person must reach hiring managers, to plan comments and connection notes
When a message asks for a favour and gives the reader no reason to care

tasks.task: Write networking messages and prepare for a first meeting

items.when: When asking for a chat, to write a short note tied to something true about that person
Before meeting someone who matters, to get a brief, a plan and an honest thank-you
When asked what do you do, to have a short answer and an opening question ready
When a follow-up to someone who went quiet sounds needy or sharp

tasks.task: Prepare the pay and offer conversation

items.when: When an offer is coming or has arrived and the person must talk about pay
Before naming a number, to see market ranges for the role and how a grant may be worth
When you want an opening line, calm questions and a fallback plan
The day before the call, to run through the prep sheet and what could go wrong
When the person plans to argue their worth and has not thought about the employer's limits

tasks.task: Build the case for a pay rise or promotion

items.when: When the person will ask their current employer for more
When results are known, to get the case, a script and replies to likely answers
Before the ask, to turn the year's work notes into evidence
When there are written promotion criteria, to match evidence to each and list the gaps
When the ask rides on a self-assessment, to write it from real examples

tasks.task: Weigh a job offer and check its terms

items.when: When an offer letter arrives, to flag risky terms and non-compete limits for a lawyer
When the full contract arrives, to get the risky terms in plain English
When the person cannot choose between two offers or between staying and going
When a deadline or flattery is pushing the person to say yes today
When the terms are weak and the person will ask for changes before signing

tasks.task: Resign well: the letter, the talk and the handover

items.when: When a new job is accepted in writing and the person must resign
When you want a second version in another tone to choose from
When the person wants to leave a note the next person can run from on day one
When the person is leaving to work for their own clients, not for another employer

tasks.task: Shape a career change story and plan the move

items.when: When the person keeps being asked why the change and needs a true, short answer
When the new field needs skills the person lacks, to plan what to learn in what order
When weighing whether to retrain, lean on others, start small or drop the idea
When the change is from a salary to the person's own clients
When the person plans one big leap and could test the new work in a small way first

tasks.task: Plan the job search and check adverts for scams

items.when: When a person starts a search or has one job they want to win
At the start of a search, or when weeks of applications have brought no interviews
When an advert looks odd, to see what it really asks for and what is missing
When time and savings are limited, to compare two ways of running the search

tasks.task: Run the weekly job search review

items.when: Once a week during an active search, in about 30 minutes with the person
When open loops and stalled applications need closing and next week needs a plan
When replies or interviews dried up, to rank the likely causes before changing everything

tasks.task: Plan the first weeks in a new job

items.when: Before meeting a new manager or team, to plan the first conversations
When the person wants draft 30, 60 and 90 day goals to agree with their manager
When the new job is a leadership role and the team needs a first note

always.when: Before anything goes to an employer, to tie every date, title and number to the person's own record
Before any CV, letter or message is sent, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the person needs to know how the hiring side screens and scores for this kind of role
When an interview talk or a speaker introduction must work read aloud
When the interview task needs slides or the CV needs a designed layout
When the person wants a run of LinkedIn posts or articles in their own voice
When the move is into a first leadership role and the question is how to lead, not how to get hired
When the question is about notice, contracts or rights at work in a given country

gaps: No library item builds a story bank of a person's own work examples in a set format
No library item answers selection criteria or public sector application questions within word limits
No library item runs a full mock interview for non-technical roles with scored feedback
No library item writes a professional bio in three lengths or a speaker one-sheet and host introduction
No library item writes a freelance marketplace profile or a service listing
No library item checks a job advert or recruiter message for scam signs
No library item writes a thank-you or follow-up message after an interview
No library item explains an employment gap, a redundancy or a short job on a CV
No library item compares two job offers on pay, benefits, travel and prospects side by side
No library item prepares a short talk for an interview presentation task, or makes clearly different CV layouts to compare
No library item helps a person choose a career direction from their strengths and interests
